title: A five minute recording exports in less time than it plays
goal: Writing a five minute screen recording out as a 1080p video takes nearly six minutes, longer than the recording itself runs. Premiere and share tools write a screen recording several times faster than it plays; people should not wait longer for the file than the video lasts.
notes: Measured 2026-09-24 during the-export-sheet-lets-you-pick-the-size-of-the-v: Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/export-a-video-at-1080p-walk.json --no-build -> [20 writeVideo] five-minutes-at-1080p.mp4 is 17 MB, written in 342447 ms; it runs 319.24s at 1728 x 1080 px ... made frame by frame from the document. Load average about 3-4 at the time. Path: EditorState.writeVideo -> DocumentFrames (composites every frame at canvas size 2880x1800, then DocumentMovieWriter fits to plan.size). Likely wins: composite at the output size rather than the canvas size, decode with hardware, pipeline frame fetch and encode. An untouched recording at Full is still a verbatim copy and is not affected.
acceptance: The five minute Retina talk, with captions burned in, writes at 1080p in under half its running time on this Mac
The export card still moves smoothly and the editor stays responsive while it writes
export-a-video-at-1080p-walk logs the time the write took and still lands a 1728 x 1080 file
